```{python}
import sys
sys.path.append("../../data")
from lin301 import *
import spacy
import unicodedata
import nltk
from nltk.corpus import wordnet as wn
```
This code imports the functions of the LIN301 python file. It also imports what's needed for the project. 
```{python}
en_words = load_words("macbeth_en.txt")
el_words = load_words("macbeth_el.txt")
fi_words = load_words("macbeth_fi.txt")
```
This code loads the words from each version of Macbeth. I also printed the first 30 words of each version. 
```{python}
nlp_en = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
en = book_to_spacy_df("macbeth_en.txt", "English", nlp_en, "ACT")
print(len(en))
print(en)
```
This code creates a spaCy Dataframe for the English version of Macbeth.
```{python}
nlp_fi = spacy.load("fi_core_news_sm")
fi = book_to_spacy_df("macbeth_fi.txt", "Finnish", nlp_fi, ".*NÄYTÖS")
print(len(fi))
print(fi)
```
This code creates a spaCy Dataframe for the Finnish version of Macbeth.
```{python}
nlp_el = spacy.load("el_core_news_sm")
el = book_to_spacy_df("macbeth_el.txt", "Greek", nlp_el, "ΠΡΑΞΙΣ")
print(len(el))
print(el)
```
This code creates a spaCy Dataframe for the Greek version of Macbeth.
```{python}
for df in [en, fi, el]:
    print(df["text"][0], round((df["pos"] == "PRON").mean() * 1000, 1))
```
This code prints the percentage of pronouns in each version. 
```{python}
for df in [en, fi, el]:
    print(df["text"][0], round((df["pos"] == "ADJ").mean() * 1000, 1))
```
This code prints the percentage of adjectives in each version.
```{python}
for df in [en, fi, el]:
    print(df["text"][0], round((df["pos"] == "NOUN").mean() * 1000, 1))
```
This code prints the amount of nouns per 1000 words in each version. 
The largest difference is the greater amount of nouns in the Finnish version compared to English and Greek. This may me because Finnish has a larger noun to parts of speech ratio. 
```{python}
el_nouns = el[el["pos"] == "NOUN"]
print("Feminine:", el_nouns["morph"].str.contains("Gender=Fem").sum())
print("Masculine:", el_nouns["morph"].str.contains("Gender=Masc").sum())
print("Neuter:", el_nouns["morph"].str.contains("Gender=Neut").sum())
```
This code prints the number of feminine, masculine, and neuter nouns in the Greek version of Macbeth.
English doesn't overtly have gendered nouns, however there are some exceptions (actor vs actress) 

I think the main differences in the three versions is due to the language. The Finnish version has a much lower word count than the other versions, this may be due to Finnish being a highly inflected language. Also, English has a larger pronoun ratio than the Finnish and Greek versions. This may be because English is inflected much less compared to Finnish and Greek.
